meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. or Mr. Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'll be direct. My son's mark was changed to a zero, he found out on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me. Why?

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Your own procedure says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered. So the zero comes out today, and then you tell me what you actually have.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Go ahead. Turn the screen so I can read it. I'm writing down what I see.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

Show me the timestamps again. 11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing them down.

And Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend. So is there anything earlier than the twenty-eighth, Hale, or is that the whole history?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.

Okay. A blank history proves when words appeared, Hale. It doesn't prove who typed them. But I can read a timestamp, so whatever happens next stays off his record and stays quiet. What else do you have?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale. That's called revising. But I want both documents in front of me, the outline with the date on it and the essay, and then you tell me exactly what you're proposing.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'm searching it now, and I'm writing down the act and scene. A misquoted line is a misquoted line, Hale, and it doesn't tell me who wrote it. Your procedure has a supervised reassessment in 4.4, so if that's what you're offering, it's private, it's not in front of his class, and "nothing goes on file" is in writing before he sits down.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Okay. Then say the terms out loud, Hale: what he writes, where, who supervises, and what replaces the zero.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Hand it to me. I want the date, the time limit and the mark on it, because forty minutes in a classroom and a take-home essay aren't the same thing. And you still haven't answered me on the terms.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Fine. I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything wrong. It's private, it's not in front of his class, the new mark replaces the zero, and "nothing goes on file" is in an email to me and the principal tonight. Until then, the zero comes off the gradebook.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Ten minutes. Which day, how long does he get, and is anyone besides you in the room? And I haven't heard you say the zero comes off the gradebook today.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

I've told you already, Hale, and I'm not going to do your job for you. The zero comes off today, the rewrite is private with a date and a time limit I can see in writing, and "nothing goes on file" is in an email to me and the principal tonight. Say yes or no to each.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
An email, okay. Does it say the zero is off the gradebook today, the date and time limit for the rewrite, and the principal copied on "nothing goes on file"? You've answered one of three.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
You're asking me to write your email, Hale. Put in 4.4, that the new mark replaces the zero, and that no one else in his class hears about this. Then answer my three questions.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight o'clock. I'm writing that down. And the zero, Hale: does it come off the gradebook before I leave this room?
Thank you for coming in.
We're not finished. You still haven't answered me on the zero, and I'm not leaving until you have.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Tomorrow at lunch. Okay, I'm writing that down. That's the rewrite, Hale. I asked about the zero, and I'll keep asking until I hear "yes" or "no."
